entities.name: Query Env gp160
observations: 768-aa viral envelope glycoprotein sequence with one ambiguous X residue.
Strong homology to reviewed HIV-1 Env gp160 proteins: 75.4–79.4% identity and approximately 99–100% query coverage.
Pfam domains: GP120 at residues 32–138 and 145–496; GP41 at residues 515–706.
Sequence architecture is consistent with an N-terminal signal peptide, large extracellular gp120-like region, gp41-like fusion region, one C-terminal transmembrane helix, and a cytoplasmic tail.

entities.name: HIV-1 Env gp160
observations: Reviewed HIV-1 Env gp160 is synthesized as a precursor, glycosylated in the secretory pathway, and cleaved by furin-like proteases into gp120 and gp41.
Mature Env forms a homotrimer of noncovalently associated gp120-gp41 heterodimers.
Gp120 mediates attachment to CD4 and subsequent coreceptor engagement; gp41 is a class I viral fusion protein.
Localized to the viral envelope and host-cell/endosomal membranes as a single-pass type I membrane protein.

entities.name: Env gp160 identification
observations: The query is most consistent with an HIV-1 group M Env gp160 envelope glycoprotein rather than a cellular receptor or enzyme.
The sequence contains numerous cysteines and NXS/T-like sequons in the ectodomain, supporting a disulfide-stabilized, heavily glycosylated viral surface protein.
Exact subtype, receptor-coreceptor usage, cleavage position, and antigenic phenotype cannot be established from this sequence alone.
